name: Setting powder

lead: Setting powder is a loose or pressed face powder applied over foundation and concealer to lock makeup in place and absorb oil. Translucent versions mainly reduce shine, and finishing powders soften the look of fine lines and pores.
It gives a more even, matte skin surface for the day, which is why it appears in grooming routines for photos and events.

paras: It is pressed or lightly dusted with a brush or sponge over areas that get oily, such as the forehead, nose and chin. Loose powder is used to set makeup, and pressed powder is used for touch-ups.
Heavy application can look clotted. Wikipedia notes that toxic ingredients are rare in modern face powders, and that historic powders sometimes contained lead.

angle.text: It gives a matte finish and helps makeup stay in place. The effect is cosmetic and lasts for as long as the powder is worn.

lead: Setting powder is a face powder used to set liquid and cream makeup so it stays in place and shines less.[1] Loose powder has a fine texture and light coverage and absorbs oil, while pressed powder in a compact suits touch-ups and can act as light foundation.[1]

Common ingredients include starch, talc, silica, zinc oxide, titanium dioxide, kaolin and dimethicone.[1] Face powder dates back to ancient Egypt, and lead-based historic powders prompted the US Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act of 1938.[1]

paras: The main types are loose, pressed, mineral, translucent, HD and finishing powder; finishing powder is described as minimising the look of fine lines and pores.[1]
Overuse of pressed powder with larger particles can look clotted.[1] Toxic ingredients are described as rare in modern face powders.[1]

timeline.event: US Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act follows lead-powder concerns.[1]
